rounds.text: Vistar Amar Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 13.5x and a price-to-book ratio of 2.32x [E1, E2], backed by robust return metrics including an ROCE of 25.5% and an ROE of 18.9% [E6, E7]. The business demonstrates extraordinary top-line and bottom-line momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 487% and profit growth of 736% [E11, E15]. This fundamental strength is reinforced by a pristine balance sheet featuring zero debt, with borrowings remaining flat at Rs 0 Cr [E32, E33]. Valuation models further underscore a significant disconnect between price and intrinsic value, as a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 638 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 65.7% [E37, E38]. Moreover, the current market price implies an earnings growth expectation of only 3.2%, which stands in stark contrast to the 18.0% base-case assumption [E39], while the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong 85 out of 100 rating [E57]. Conceded: [E28].

The most pressing risk facing Vistar Amar Ltd is the severe disconnect between its reported profits and actual cash generation, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.33x and operating cash flow representing only 42% of operating profit for March 2026 [E28, E31]. This shortfall leaves the company with a negative free cash flow of Rs -2 Cr [E30] and is compounded by worsening working capital metrics, specifically debtor days expanding significantly from 61.5 to 88.9 days [E56]. Furthermore, operational quality is plagued by inconsistency, with both yearly and quarterly operating margin trends labeled as inconsistent [E26, E27], and a low 3-year median return on equity of 12.2% [E55]. Shareholders also receive no immediate cash return, as the dividend yield sits entirely at 0.00% [E4], while the stock itself carries immense structural risk marked by an annualized volatility of 58.3% and a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.7% [E45, E46]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong compounding sales and profit growth over various trailing periods, maintains zero debt, and trades at an attractive P/E of 13.5x with a favorable baseline return on capital employed [E1, E6, E8, E11, E12, E15, E32].

Conceded: cash conversion is 0.33x and free cash flow is Rs -2 Cr in Mar 2026 [E28, E30]. However, the business operates with zero debt (Rs 0 Cr borrowings, 0.00x debt to equity), entirely neutralizing the liquidity threat typically associated with temporary working capital friction [E32, E33, E51]. The broader fundamental engine completely overwhelms short-term margin noise, delivering a robust 25.5% ROCE and a 5-year profit CAGR of 33.3%, which vastly outperforms the sector median profit growth of 16.7% [E6, E52, E65]. Conceded: debtor days expanded to 88.9 days [E56], but offsetting this, working capital requirements have structurally improved over the longer term, dropping from 129 days down to 67.5 days [E54]. Furthermore, the market is pricing this high-growth profile at an undemanding P/E of just 13.5x while profit growth vastly outpaces 1-year price performance by 668%, backed by a rules-based screen score of 85 out of 100 [E1, E49, E57].

Conceded: borrowings are zero at Rs 0 Cr and debt-to-equity is 0.00x [E32, E33]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash generation friction ignores that cash conversion stands at a meager 0.33x and free cash flow dropped to Rs -2 Cr in Mar 2026, meaning reported profits are not translating into actual liquidity [E28, E30]. While the bull highlights long-term working capital improvement, debtor days have actively deteriorated from 61.5 to 88.9 days, directly contradicting the narrative of smooth operational efficiency [E54, E56]. Conceded: 5-year profit CAGR is 33.3% and ROCE is 25.5% [E6, E52]. Yet, the earnings profile is explicitly classified as cyclical, with historical performance marked by a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.7% and annualised volatility of 58.3%, alongside an inconsistent annual operating-margin trend over the last two years [E26, E45, E46, E50]. Finally, the screen engine explicitly warns that earnings growth is decelerating, tempering the enthusiasm behind the bull's rear-view growth metrics [E62].
